answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a triangulated lattice: an identity only counts when three unrelated peers vouch for it, peers who never vouched for each other and earned standing in different epochs. Like basalt, the lattice is hard to crack from one side; like a juniper, real reputation grows slowly; like water through karst, trust seeps along many small channels no farm can flood at once. Fakes can only vouch for each other, forming a tight clique the check rejects, while honest agents gather endorsements at work, so fakery costs real history and honesty costs almost nothing.
